Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Financial Group Fourth Quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, if you have a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Apex Financial Group's results for the fourth quarter. With me this morning are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer; Robert Hayes, Chief Risk Officer; Jennifer Kim, Chief Credit Officer; and Amit Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Financial Group delivered excellent results in the fourth quarter, demonstrating the strength of our franchise and our ability to navigate a dynamic market environment.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on expanding our market share through targeted growth in high-potential regions, improving our efficiency ratio toward the low 50s, strengthening our balance sheet with robust capital levels, investing in our people to foster a high-performance culture, driving innovation via cutting-edge technology platforms, and meeting our ESG goals with expanded sustainable financing commitments.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on key areas of performance. First, our net interest income showed strong momentum, with year-over-year growth of 18% and sequential expansion, supported by asset yield improvements and deposit optimization. Credit quality held resilient, with non-performing loan ratios below peer averages and controlled charge-offs across segments. Non-interest income benefited from favorable market conditions, including elevated volatility and M&A activity, contributing meaningfully to revenue diversity. Our technology investments are paying off handsomely, driving efficiency gains and a sharply improved cost-to-income ratio. Looking ahead, we're providing constructive guidance for net interest income and earnings in the coming quarter. Finally, against a macroeconomic backdrop of moderating inflation and anticipated rate adjustments, we're well-positioned to deliver through-the-cycle performance.

I will now turn the call over to Emily Carter to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, Mark, and good morning. Apex Financial Group reported net income of $850 million for the fourth quarter, or $2.10 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 18% year-over-year and 4.2% quarter-over-quarter to $2.85 billion, with full-year NII reaching $11.2 billion, up 22% from 2022, surpassing our initial guidance as we adeptly managed Fed funds rate hikes to 5.25-5.50% and their lagged effects on our funding mix. Breaking down the year-over-year trends, this robust increase stemmed from significant balance sheet growth and yield enhancement. Average earning assets expanded 12% to $285 billion, propelled by 15% growth in our loan portfolio, particularly in commercial and industrial lending to $120 billion and steady mortgage banking originations of $45 billion even at 7% mortgage rates. Asset yields rose 145 basis points to 5.85%, aided by faster repricing on variable-rate loans, now 62% of total loans up from 55%, with C&I yields climbing 210 basis points to 6.75% through disciplined pricing comparable to peers like JPMorgan and Wells Fargo.

On liabilities, funding costs increased more gradually to 2.40% all-in deposit cost, a 110 basis point rise but under the industry beta of 45% per FDIC data, thanks to deposit optimization like our high-yield Apex Digital Savings product launched in Q2, which attracted $18 billion in low-cost core deposits at 3.85%, lifting non-interest-bearing deposits to 28% of funding from 24%. Our loan-to-deposit ratio stayed healthy at 82%, ensuring strong liquidity.

Sequentially, the 4.2% growth from $2.735 billion in Q3 represented our sixth straight quarter of NII expansion, countering seasonal patterns, driven by 3% growth in earning assets to $288 billion from $5 billion in new C&I commitments linked to Inflation Reduction Act infrastructure financing. Net interest margin widened 8 basis points to 3.95%, the highest in two years, as asset repricing outran deposit betas. Our $40 billion investment portfolio of variable-rate securities like Agency MBS and corporates saw 25 basis point repricing gains, complemented by derisking via $2.2 billion sale of lower-yielding held-to-maturity securities for a $150 million after-tax gain to support capital.

Regionally, U.S. Consumer & Business Banking led with 25% YoY NII growth to $1.4 billion, aided by deposit betas under 40% in our top-5 Southeast market share. Europe via London and Frankfurt hubs grew 12% YoY to €650 million ($710 million) but dipped 2% QoQ due to ECB's 4% terminal rate and €3 billion deposit outflows to money market funds at 4.5%. Asia-Pacific, 15% of NII, advanced 10% YoY on trade finance in Singapore and Hong Kong, though QoQ slowed to 1% amid China property challenges similar to HSBC's.

Strategically, our ALCO hedging deployed $10 billion in interest rate swaps at 4.75% receive-fixed, protecting 30% of the balance sheet from projected 2024 rate cuts per CME FedWatch. Digital deposit growth via Apex Mobile added 1.2 million accounts at under $50 acquisition cost, emulating Ally and SoFi. We're reshaping securities toward shorter-duration floaters for 20 basis points NIM uplift in 2024. For next year, we guide NII to $11.8-12.2 billion, or 5-9% growth, with NIM at 3.90-4.05%. Risks include accelerated deposit repricing or competition, but $45 billion cash equivalents and 11.8% CET1 enable opportunistic lending, plus $200 million run-rate NII from our pending $1.2 billion regional bank acquisition.

Turning to non-interest income, we generated $2.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 28% of total revenue, highlighting the durability of our fee businesses despite macro shifts. Key tailwinds included equity volatility, global M&A resurgence, and transaction banking strength, offset somewhat by normalizing FX and softer mortgage fees from persistent high rates. Our CIB and Wealth Management drove 55% and 25% respectively.

Investment banking fees hit $850 million, up 32% YoY, as M&A volumes reached $1.2 trillion per Dealogic, highest since Q4 2022, with us advising 15 deals over $1 billion like a $45 billion U.S.-European semiconductor merger under antitrust review. Underwriting ranked us #3 globally with $25 billion ECM/DCM, 8% high-yield share amid refinancing post-525 basis point Fed hikes. Advisory surged 45% on cross-border prowess; Americas 60%, APAC 25%, EMEA 15% held back by U.K. regulations.

Markets trading revenues of $650 million rose 12% YoY, fueled by VIX at 22 driving rates, FX, equities flow. FICC up 15% to $420 million on Treasury yield swings 4.2-4.8% and EUR/USD 450 pips; equities $230 million up 8% on AI hedge fund activity. Inventory managed well with minor $25 million unrealized dip versus Goldman's larger hits; our Apex algo suite handled 65% flows, adding 50 basis points margins at sub-100 microsecond latency.

Wealth and asset management fees of $720 million grew 14% YoY as AUM hit $1.9 trillion up 10% on S&P 12% returns. Annuity/advisory up 16% with $45 billion net inflows to 9-11% private credit; performance fees $120 million. U.S. +18%, Europe +5%, APAC +22% via family offices. AI Horizon platform serves 2.5 million clients, boosting retention to 97% and cross-sell 15%.

Payments, cards, others at $480 million up 9% YoY: card spend +11% for $280 million interchange; Treasury Services $4.5 trillion up 13%; FX $140 million down 5% QoQ. Diversification now buffers 35% of earnings from NII pressures, backed by $500 million cloud/blockchain investments cutting settlement 40% via Swift GPI. APAC Mumbai hub targets India's $5 trillion payments. Q4 guide $2.7-2.9 billion assuming VIX 18-20.

Our technology investments amplified efficiency, with $1.2 billion FY23 spend up 18% YoY or 8% of opex, matching JPM/Wells peers. 45% infrastructure like AWS/GCP Temenos migration for 95% STP on loans/deposits, slashing mortgage times to 10 days from 45. RPA via UiPath automated 40% back-office for $180 million savings; gen AI with Palantir/Snowflake cut fraud $120 million.

North America APIs via Plaid added 8% deposits; EMEA cybersecurity for PSD3/DORA; APAC mobile for 30% volumes. CIR fell 450 bps to 54%, best since 2019, vs industry 58%; revenue/FTE +11% to $285k; headcount -7%; costs/transaction -22% to $0.45. FY24 $1.4 billion spend targets sub-52% CIR via gen AI service (35% faster) and Ripple blockchain.

We're on track for full-year financial targets.

Robert Hayes:
Thank you, Emily. From a risk perspective, we are closely monitoring macroeconomic factors and credit migration risks. The IMF projects 3.2% global GDP for 2024 amid supply disruptions and geopolitics; U.S. CPI at 3.0%, Eurozone 2.5%. Fed steady at 5.25-5.50% with two cuts eyed, ECB at 3.75%, PBOC easing for China's 4.8%.

This supports our 3.45% NIM up 12 bps on 70% variable loans at 5.2% SOFR, deposit betas 65%; cuts may trim 5-10 bps, hedged by ALM and 4.1% yielding securities duration 2.8 years. Loans +5.2% YoY selective in tech/renewables; provisions $450 million up 15% QoQ, CECL 1.15%, NPLs 0.85% mainly office CRE $12 billion (2% total), CCAR stress-tested. CET1 12.8% enables $2-3 billion buybacks.

U.S. 55% revenues: consumer +2.8%, $1.2 trillion payments +12%, gen AI cash tools +15% retention. Europe 25%: iFAST AUM +9% on MiFID/ESG. APAC 20%: India/ASEAN apps +2.5 million, remittances +18% RippleNet. Initiatives: $500 million AWS core -25% TCO, ML PD/LGD -30% false positives, $10 billion green loans +50 bps ROTCE, fintech M&A. FY24 EPS $8.50-8.80 mid-single digits; LDR 92%, LCR 145%. We're vigilant on credit/deposits but fortified.

Jennifer Kim:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains strong with non-performing loans at 98 basis points, up 5 bps sequentially from 93 but down 15 bps YoY from 113, below 120 bps through-cycle average and peers Wells 102 bps, BofA 105 bps per SNL.

Delinquencies at 1.85% improved 10 bps QoQ/25 bps YoY; 30-59 days 1.12% seasonal cards, 60-89 0.73%. Net charge-offs 62 bps annualized up from 58 QoQ but flat YoY; core ex-PCI 55 bps.

Consumer $150 billion: auto delinq 2.1% from 2.4% via 720 FICO, Ally subprime cap 15%; cards NCO 3.2% on 28% utilization offset by EagleEye AI collections 45 days early; NPLs 1.2%.

Residential $120 billion 60% GSE: NPLs 0.8% lowest in 5Q on Sun Belt LTV 65%; delinq 0.9%; ALLL 210% NPLs.

C&I $100 billion: NPLs 65 bps down 20 bps YoY, delinq 0.6% on investment-grade 85%, Midwest strength; criticized 2.8% tech/healthcare.

CRE $80 billion 18% total, office 25%: NPLs 1.8% up 30 bps urban remote work; NCO 120 bps incl $45 million Manhattan charges like NYCB; Northeast 35% cap rates 7.5% CBRE, Sun Belt multifamily 0.4%; sold $2.5 billion office at 95 cents, concentration 4.5%; Moody's CECL +15%.

Provisions $250 million 45 bps down from $320 million Q1; ALLL $4.2 billion 1.05% loans, 420% NPLs, stress +100 bps Fed ok.

Regions: Southeast/Southwest 40% footprint NPLs 75 bps migration/energy; Northeast +20 bps CRE/consumer; Europe London C&I 1.1% ECB cuts.

GenAI Falcon 92% 90-day delinq accuracy +25%, Plaid/Experian data 70% dynamic pricing; omnichannel collections +15% recovery. Diversify to equipment +12% Caterpillar/John Deere, SBA 7(a). Stress 50 bps cut -10 bps NPLs. Vs 2023 turmoil, CET1 11.8% LCR 145%. FY24 NCOs 60-70 bps, NPLs <100 bps; CECL/$1.2 billion undrawn buffer.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you have a question at this time, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Doe:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the NII trends, particularly the drivers behind the sustained sequential growth?

Mark Thompson:
Thanks, John. As Emily detailed, our NII trajectory reflects a well-executed strategy in a rising rate world transitioning potentially to cuts. The 18% YoY and 4.2% QoQ growth to $2.85 billion was powered by 12% earning asset expansion to $285 billion, 145 bps yield lift to 5.85% on 62% variable loans, and controlled deposit costs at 2.40% via digital products like Apex Savings gathering $18 billion core. QoQ, infrastructure C&I added momentum, NIM to 3.95%, portfolio repositioning, and hedging $10 billion swaps at 4.75%. Regional strengths in U.S. Southeast offset Europe outflows. This positions us for 2024 guide of $11.8-12.2 billion with fortress liquidity.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith:
What is your strategy for technology investments and their impact on efficiency going forward?

Emily Carter:
Great question, Jane. Our FY23 $1.2 billion tech outlay, 18% up and 8% opex, funds modernization mirroring top peers. Cloud migration to AWS/GCP Temenos hit 95% STP, mortgage times to 10 days; RPA UiPath $180 million savings; gen AI Palantir/Snowflake fraud cuts $120 million. Regional: NA Plaid APIs +8% deposits; EMEA CrowdStrike DORA; APAC mobile +30% volumes. Delivered 54% CIR, +11% rev/FTE, -22% transaction costs. FY24 $1.4 billion targets sub-52%, gen AI 50% service, Ripple blockchain -40% SWIFT. This flywheel sustains 12-14% ROTCE amid Basel IV/inflation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Brown with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Brown:
How are you addressing macroeconomic headwinds and their potential impact on risk?

Robert Hayes:
Thanks, Mike. Our diversified model across NA/Europe/APAC leverages IMF 3.2% global GDP, U.S. CPI 3%, Fed/ECB easing paths. NIM 3.45% asset-sensitive buffered by hedges; loans +5.2% selective; CECL 1.15% provisions up. U.S. consumer/capex strong for fees; Europe iFAST ESG; APAC digital boom. $500 million AWS, ML risk -30% positives, $10B green, fintech M&A fortify. CET1 12.8%, LCR 145% for outperformance in cuts/recession avoidance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Green with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Green:
Can you update us on credit quality trends, especially in CRE?

Jennifer Kim:
Absolutely, Lisa. NPLs 98 bps down YoY/below peers, delinq 1.85% improved, NCO 62 bps core 55 bps. Consumer auto 2.1%, cards AI offset; resi 0.8%; C&I 65 bps; CRE 1.8% office up but de-risked $2.5B sales to 4.5% conc, Moody's stress. Provisions 45 bps, ALLL 420% NPLs. GenAI Falcon 92% accuracy, collections +15%, diversify equipment/SBA. FY24 NCO 60-70 bps stable.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Mark Thompson for any closing remarks.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you for your interest in Apex Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
